think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 50-year-old male with acute lymphoblastic leukemia who underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation (SCT) presents 12 months post-transplant with fluctuating, mild cytopenias—predominantly isolated thrombocytopenia (60–80 × 10^9/L)—and intermittent fatigue. In a post-transplant patient on immunosuppression with a prior history of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), persistent thrombocytopenia strongly raises suspicion for leukemic relapse, graft failure, GVHD recurrence, or opportunistic viral reactivation (CMV/EBV). The clinical dilemma is recognizing occult protozoal marrow infiltration in an afebrile, clinically stable allograft recipient.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint is set at the 12-month post-SCT outpatient evaluation when the patient presents with fluctuating thrombocytopenia, complete donor chimerism, and negative clinical/laboratory screens for GVHD, common viral/bacterial infections, and leukemic relapse, immediately before the routine surveillance bone marrow aspirate smear and Leishmania infantum DNA PCR results are disclosed.
3. Differential Distinctions: GVHD recurrence is ruled out by the absence of active gastrointestinal, hepatic, or skin lesions. Leukemic relapse and secondary myelodysplasia are excluded by persistent 100% donor chimerism and absence of blasts/dysplasia on bone marrow surveillance.
case_prompt:
A 50-year-old male with high-risk acute lymphoblastic B-cell leukemia in first complete remission presents for scheduled post-transplantation outpatient surveillance 12 months after undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation (SCT). The transplant was performed with peripheral blood stem cells from an unrelated Portuguese matched 9/10 donor (mismatch at the HLA-A locus) following a myeloablative conditioning regimen of busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and antilymphocytic serum. Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis had consisted of tacrolimus and methotrexate. His post-transplant course was complicated at 2 months by upper digestive GVHD, which was successfully treated with systemic corticosteroids.

Over the subsequent months, the patient developed mild, fluctuating cytopenias, predominantly thrombocytopenia with platelet counts persistently hovering between 60 and 80 × 10^9/L. His only reported symptom is intermittent fatigue. He denies fevers, chills, night sweats, anorexia, weight loss, mucosal bleeding, petechiae, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or diarrhea.

On physical examination, he appears well, afebrile, and hemodynamically stable. There is no pallor, jaundice, peripheral lymphadenopathy, petechial rash, or mucosal lesions. Abdominal examination is soft and non-tender without palpable hepatosplenomegaly. Diagnostic workup for common secondary etiologies of post-transplant thrombocytopenia confirms complete donor chimerism. There is no clinical or biochemical evidence of active graft-versus-host disease, and screening for common viral (including CMV and EBV) and bacterial infections is negative. Peripheral blood examination reveals no dysplastic changes or circulating blast cells.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Because the patient had prior biopsy-confirmed upper digestive GVHD treated with corticosteroids, new or persistent cytopenias in an allogeneic graft recipient raised suspicion for immune-mediated graft dysfunction or marrow GVHD. However, comprehensive clinical, endoscopic, and laboratory examinations showed no evidence of active gastrointestinal, cutaneous, or hepatic GVHD.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The common causes for thrombocytopenia were excluded:no evidence of graft versus host disease; no signs of viral or bacterial infection; and no signs of relapsed disease/dysplastic changes.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Leukemic relapse or donor cell myelodysplastic syndrome (secondary graft failure)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Fluctuating thrombocytopenia one year after myeloablative allogeneic stem cell transplantation for high-risk B-ALL is concerning for disease recurrence or secondary myelodysplasia. However, repeat molecular testing verified stable 100% complete donor chimerism, and surveillance evaluations showed no evidence of blast infiltration or dysplastic features.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Bone marrow evaluation had no signs of relapse disease and patient had complete chimerism.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic pivot occurred when a 12-month post-transplant surveillance bone marrow smear unexpectedly revealed massive intracellular infiltration of reticuloendothelial macrophages by amastigotes showing hemophagocytosis, confirmed by PCR analysis as Leishmania infantum, with prompt hematologic recovery following liposomal amphotericin B.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The bone marrow smear performed 12 months after transplant revealed an unsuspected diagnosis: a massive bone marrow infiltration with amastigotes:(Figure 1 optical microscopy, Wright Giemsa stain, 100x magnification). Reticuloendothelial cells had exuberant parasitic cytoplasmatic inclusions and a few images of erythrophagocytosis were present (Figure 1). The sample was sent to DNA PCR analysis and Leishmania infantum was identified.

editor_comments: Presents the subtle challenge of visceral leishmaniasis manifesting as isolated post-transplant cytopenia without classic hepatosplenomegaly. Breakpoint strictly isolates marrow histology and PCR.
